title: Authorization resolves to one of three policies chosen once at boot: OPEN, ADMIN_ONLY, or DOCUMENT_PERMISSIONS
content:
## One service, selected at boot

Authorization in a Reactor is decided by a **single service selected once at boot** — not per request, not per resolver, and not per document. Two environment flags pick which service you get:

| Policy | When | What the enforcement helpers do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OPEN` | `AUTH_ENABLED=false` | Every check passes for everyone, including anonymous callers |
| `ADMIN_ONLY` | `AUTH_ENABLED=true`, document permissions off | Only addresses in `ADMINS` pass any check |
| `DOCUMENT_PERMISSIONS` | `DOCUMENT_PERMISSIONS_ENABLED=true` | Full per-document protection plus READ/WRITE/ADMIN grants, with inheritance |

`AUTH_ENABLED=false` bypasses every authorization check, which is why the docs call it development-only.

## The consequence for builders

Because the policy is resolved centrally, the correct approach in a custom subgraph is to **write one enforcement path** and let it behave correctly under all three policies. A helper call is always safe:

```typescript
const handle = await subgraph.assertCanRead(args.identifier, ctx);
return subgraph.reactorClient.get(handle.fetchIdentifier);
```

Under `OPEN` that assert is effectively a no-op. Under `ADMIN_ONLY` and `DOCUMENT_PERMISSIONS` it fails closed. Either way the resolver reads the same.

The rule that falls out of this is stated as a best practice: **write the check unconditionally**. Do not special-case `OPEN` or `ADMIN_ONLY` in a resolver — the helpers already collapse to the correct behaviour per policy, and a resolver that tries to detect the policy itself is both redundant and a place for the two implementations to drift apart.

The policy type is exported as `AuthorizationPolicy` from `@powerhousedao/reactor-api` when you need to name it, but needing to name it in a resolver is usually a sign the enforcement path is being written twice.

description: AUTH_ENABLED=false gives OPEN, auth on without document permissions gives ADMIN_ONLY, DOCUMENT_PERMISSIONS_ENABLED=true gives full grants. Resolvers never branch on policy.
